Backend: 15/15 iter3 pytest cases passing (Schedule CRUD + create/list/get/toggle/delete + run-now, cron scheduler dispatch within ~90s, one-shot fires once and disables, checkpoint GET/DELETE + stats accuracy, discovery annotation with checkpoint_status, delta/incremental filter behavior in POST /jobs including failed-item retry). Regression: 42/42 iter1+iter2 tests still passing (total 57/57). Frontend: Sidebar 'Schedules' nav link works and navigates to /app/schedules; New Schedule modal opens, cron preset+input work, discover picks up items, submitting creates schedule (toast shows next-run) and row shows Run/Pause/Delete controls; ServiceModule checkpoint banner shows 3 ok · 0 err · 3 tracked after a real 3-item exchange job, LAST SYNC timestamp populates, per-row green 'success' badges render in Sync column, hide-already-synced toggle filters (64→61).

issues: Scheduler status indicator '● SCHEDULER ONLINE · TICK 15S' in the table header is clear and green — good design touch. Row status shows 'RUNNING' badge in cyan when the schedule has an active/last job; consider adding a separate 'IDLE' vs 'PAUSED' distinction (currently paused schedules would just fall out of the enabled=true filter — check if UI renders them differently).
Layout is clean: LAST SYNC | CHECKPOINT counts | hide-already-synced checkbox | RESET CHECKPOINT button. Color coding (green ok, red err, zinc tracked) reads well. No accessibility issues observed.

action_items: No blocking action items. All iteration-3 features working as designed.

Optional (dev-only): The preview environment editor still injects <span> nodes inside <option> tags on SchedulesPage.jsx (concurrency/mode/service selects) causing a React hydration warning in the console — NOT in source code; same tooling artifact noted in iteration 2. Ignorable.

Optional: On SchedulesPage the disabled/paused state is not visually distinguished from a running-but-not-yet-fired schedule (both fall out of the RUNNING pill). Consider adding a PAUSED badge in gray when enabled=false so users can tell at a glance.
critical_code_review_comments: scheduler.py:100 — the tick query `{enabled: True, next_run_at: {$lte: now_iso}}` compares ISO strings, which works because they are timezone-consistent (both produced via `_iso(_now())` in UTC). If a schedule ever ingests a run_at without tz offset, the string compare will silently misbehave. Consider storing next_run_at as a bson datetime rather than an ISO string, or normalize/validate the offset on create.

server.py:768-770 — for one_shot schedules, if the client passes run_at with a non-UTC offset (e.g., '2026-03-15T10:00:00-05:00'), `compute_next_run` returns it verbatim; the scheduler's $lte compare against '2026-03-15T15:00:00+00:00' (UTC iso) would then be a lexicographic compare between differently-offset strings which is NOT correct. Reproducible edge case. Recommend converting run_at → UTC iso on create.

checkpoints.py:62-73 — `record_item_result` upserts `last_sync_at` on every item write; this is a per-item write rather than a job-end summary write. Fine for correctness, but under a very large migration (e.g., 100k items) this becomes 100k Mongo upserts against the same doc. Consider a bulk-write buffer inside `run_job` that flushes every N items or at job end.

server.py:539-547 — delta filter re-runs `_discover(...)` inside `create_job` via the earlier `full_items` call at line 526. For very large tenants this doubles the Graph latency (once for the UI's discover call, once again here). Consider passing annotated items via body, or caching discovery per (project, service) for a few seconds.

scheduler.py:93 — `asyncio.create_task(run_job_fn(job_id))` is fire-and-forget with no error handler; unhandled exceptions inside run_job will surface as a 'Task exception was never retrieved' warning. Consider `.add_done_callback(_log_task_error)` to log the traceback cleanly.

server.py:822 — `run_schedule_now` doesn't recompute next_run_at, so a manual run can accidentally shift the natural cron cadence if the caller expects the next scheduled run to be recalculated from 'now'. Current behaviour (keep original next_run_at) is arguably correct but worth documenting.
